text:
Maya: Kicking off eu-south1 cluster-03 bring-up. Nodepool gpu-v2 bootstrap started, terraform finished. Noticed several node bootstraps failing during post-install, reporting back now. Anyone on infra can take a look? :wave:

deploy-bot: [automation] cluster-create job started for eu-south1/cluster-03 (job id c-3342)

ops-bot: terraform apply complete, VPC and subnets provisioned. Route tables and mgmt SGs in place.

Heng: seeing this in node bootstrap logs on failed instances:
```
Jul 12 03:12:02 kubelet[1234]: E0712 03:12:02.123456    1234 kubelet.go:2004] Failed to start container runtime: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to run containerd: exit status 127: /usr/bin/nvidia-container-runtime: No such file or directory
Jul 12 03:12:02 cloud-init[999]: post-install script exited 127
```

Riley: hmm we set MTU 9000 on the VPC for throughput. The CNI default / node OS uses 1500, we've seen weird pod networking flaps at 9000 if CNI isn't configured. Could be overlay fragmentation.

Samir: also seeing GPU driver mismatch in the installer logs: installer requested driver 530.x but AMI has 525. That explains missing nvidia runtime binary.

Maya: ok two separate issues (MTU/CNI + driver/runtime). Which one is the immediate blocker for bootstrap?

Heng: primary blocker is missing nvidia-container-runtime -> containerd refuses to start -> kubelet fails -> node marked NotReady. MTU will cause intermittent pod failures but nodes should still register. Recommend we fix drivers first.

Samir: quick mitigation: 1) patch bootstrap script to install nvidia-driver-525 to match AMI (or replace AMI with 530). 2) add post-boot step to install nvidia-container-runtime and restart containerd.

Maya: can someone push the patch and re-run bootstrap on a single test node? I want to avoid rolling the whole pool until we confirm.

Heng: pushing small bootstrap patch to git branch eu-south1-gpu-fix and kicking off a single node repro.

deploy-bot: [automation] terraform taint aws_instance.cluster-03-gpu-001 && apply queued (user: heng)

ops-bot: applying patch to userdata: added apt install nvidia-driver-525 && apt-get install -y nvidia-container-runtime.

Heng: test node came up but now CNI shows flaps on pods, fragmentation errors in calico logs: 
```
Jul 12 03:23:10 calico-node[456]: WARN endpoint apply failed: error writing route: file exists (mtu mismatch?)
Jul 12 03:23:11 kernel: IP: bad checksum from eth0, fragmented packet
```

Riley: confirm: calico default MTU is 1440. Our host MTU 9000 + overlay config mismatch causing kernel to drop fragments. Option A: set host MTU to 1500 on new nodes. Option B: configure CNI MTU and ipip/encap settings.

Samir: for long term we like 9000 for throughput. For immediate bring-up: set host MTU to 1500 in cloud-init metadata so controller registers healthy nodes. We'll follow up with a plan to enable jumbo frames cluster-wide after testing.

Maya: agree. Heng, can you update userdata to force MTU 1500 on eth0 and re-run single node?

Heng: updated userdata + restarted tainted instance. Node reached Ready. GPU libs present, containerd running. Pod scheduling OK.

deploy-bot: [automation] cluster rollout: started canary for nodepool gpu-v2 (3 nodes)

ops-bot: canary failed: 2/3 new nodes NotReady within 10m. Autoscaler attempted scale up and hit quota limit in eu-south1 for p4d instances. Quota request pending.

Maya: ugh quota. We should have requested quotas earlier. Is there an emergency quota increase path?

oncall-ops: filed support ticket with cloud provider (#INC-7782) but ETA 4-6 hours. Suggest we pause rollout and avoid partial capacity that causes API churn.

Samir: because canary failed and >30% of intended pool failed, deployment automation triggered a rollback per our safety policy. deploy-bot will restore previous nodepool config.

deploy-bot: [automation] rollback triggered: reason=canary_failure threshold=0.3; action=restore previous instance group (rollout id r-889).

Riley: we definitely need to update runbook: pre-check cloud quotas, AMI-driver matrix, and VPC MTU alignment. This sequence of small infra mismatches is what tripled the mean time.

Maya: Agreed. Immediate next steps: 1) open runbook PR with checklist items (quota, AMI-driver mapping, MTU) 2) follow up with cloud support on quota 3) schedule a dedicated test to validate jumbo frames end-to-end before enabling 9000.

Samir: logging action items in #infra-ops-issues board. I'll take AMI-driver mapping and add a matrix to the repo. Heng : please add the MTU fix to bootstrap templates. Riley : please draft CNI jumbo frame validation plan.

Heng: noted. I'll also add a fail-fast check in bootstrap that validates nvidia-container-runtime exists before marking node healthy (so we don't wait for scheduler churn).

Maya: thanks all. We'll hold full rollout until quota confirmed and runbook updates merged. Creating follow-up incident doc. :memo: 

oncall-ops: tagging for handoff to day shift: @Maya @Samir please coordinate morning run.

Riley: thx, will draft runbook PR this afternoon. :+1:

Maya: closing thread for now, will update when quota/PRs done.
